section: 5.1; Key Terms (Security or Securities, Deal or Dealing)
detail: An OTC put or call over Suncorp shares is a Security in its own right, so writing or buying it is a Dealing that would otherwise need clearance outside Closed Periods. But because the pair is designed to limit economic risk of a holding, section 5.1's hedging ban applies and the collar legs are prohibited outright rather than merely clearable.
evidence: derivative products (including but not limited to warrants, exchange-traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) relating to those securities, whether or not the securities or the derivative products are issued or created by Suncorp or by third parties.

detail: Exchange-traded options and warrants over Suncorp Securities are expressly within the definition of Securities, so acquiring or disposing of them is a Dealing requiring prior written clearance, outside Closed Periods and the Restricted List. Permitted only where the derivative is not itself designed to limit economic risk of a Suncorp holding (5.1) and does not amount to short-term Dealing or short selling (5.2).
evidence: Outside of Closed Periods, Prescribed Persons and their Connected Persons are required to obtain clearance before Dealing in Suncorp Securities (unless the proposed Dealing falls into an Exempt Dealing category set out in Section 3).

detail: Absolute, tier-wide hedging ban with no clearance or waiver route. It is not confined to plan or unvested securities: it reaches any 'holdings in Suncorp Securities' and expressly extends to unvested performance rights, so vested unrestricted shares are covered too. There is no venue limit and no exception for a collar.
evidence: Directors, Employees and Contractors are prohibited from entering into a hedging transaction that is designed to limit the economic risk of holdings in Suncorp Securities, including unvested performance rights.

evidence: prohibited from entering into a hedging transaction that is designed to limit the economic risk of holdings in Suncorp Securities, including unvested performance rights.

detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar-plus-loan or similar structure is designed to limit the economic risk of a Suncorp holding and so is caught by the section 5.1 hedging ban; forward contracts are also given as the example of prohibited short-term Dealing in 5.2(a).
evidence: entering into any other short term Dealings (for example, forward contracts) in relation to Securities.

detail: Outright ban for Prescribed Persons and Connected Persons, defined as borrowing the security and selling it to profit from an anticipated fall. No carve-outs and no clearance route.
evidence: Short Selling of Suncorp Securities. evidence: derivative products (including but not limited to warrants, exchange-traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) relating to those securities

The heading says Prescribed Persons 'may be restricted', so clearance is discretionary and may be refused without reasons.
evidence: The Suncorp Chairman, or the Group CEO, will review any request for waiver or clearance to Deal by Prescribed Persons or their Connected Persons which involves entering into a new or increased Margin Loan or other use of Suncorp Securities as collateral in a financial transaction.

evidence: Short-Term Dealing of Suncorp Securities: means buying and selling the same Security within a six month period and entering into any other short term Dealings (for example, forward contracts) in relation to Securities.

detail: Exchange-traded options, warrants, futures and other Financial Products issued over Scentre Group Securities and able to be traded on a financial market are themselves Scentre Group Securities, so trading them requires prior written clearance and is barred in blackout periods. Any such derivative must not be short-term or speculative under 11(d), and clearance will be refused if the request rests on short-term or speculative considerations.
evidence: any Financial Products issued over or in respect of the above securities which are able to be traded on a financial market.

detail: A bilateral OTC put and call with a bank is arguably outside limb (d) of Scentre Group Securities, which is confined to Financial Products 'able to be traded on a financial market', so the clearance and blackout machinery may not reach it on its own terms. But 11(d) expressly regulates 'derivative or other Financial Products issued over or in respect of Scentre Group Securities' without that market-traded limitation, and Financial Product expressly includes options, forward contracts and swaps. The prudent and evidently intended reading is that an OTC collar is caught and needs clearance; it is prohibited if short-term or speculative.
evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or is respect of Scentre Group Securities.

Hedging them is regulated only as trading: prior written clearance from the relevant Clearance Officer, outside blackout periods, not short-term or speculative, and subject to whatever the separate Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy says.
evidence: Prohibitions also apply to executives participating in the equity-linked incentive plans from entering into hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards or awards that have vested but are held in a holding lock or otherwise the subject of deferral of delivery

evidence: “deal” or “trade” includes to take part in any transaction associated with buying, selling, acquiring, disposing of, converting or agreeing to do any of those things

evidence: Financial Product means any financial instrument, including derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference.

detail: Flat ban on entering margin lending arrangements in relation to Scentre Group Securities, with no clearance or waiver route. evidence: Restricted Persons may not enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to Scentre Group Securities.

detail: Granting a security interest over Scentre Group Securities is not a 'trade' under the deal/trade definition and is not caught by the margin lending ban, but the policy imposes a standalone requirement of prior approval from the Company Secretary before entering into any such security arrangement. evidence: However, if a Restricted Person proposes to enter into any such security arrangement they should obtain the prior approval of the Company Secretary prior to entering into any such arrangement.

detail: The policy draws an express and unusual line: the ban stops at margin lending and does not extend to other types of loan secured by a security interest over Scentre Group Securities. evidence: The above restriction includes all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements but does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Scentre Group Securities.

detail: Short-term or speculative trading is banned in Scentre Group Securities and in derivatives or other Financial Products issued over or in respect of them; short-term means in less than a 3-month period. evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or is respect of Scentre Group Securities. Short-term means in less than a 3-month period.

evidence: any derivatives of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.

detail: The policy contains no hedging prohibition and no definition of hedging or of limiting economic risk. evidence: any derivatives of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.

evidence: Deal or Dealing means, in relation to any PME Security, to apply for, acquire, convert or dispose of that PME Security, or agreeing to, inciting, procuring or inducing any person or entity to do so.
